title: Oliver's band personnel and the reed and trombone changes
summary: After a Lincoln Gardens fire, he lists Buster Bailey, Rudy Jackson, Charlie Jackson on bass sax, and the trombone changes; Bigard, Nicholas and Louis Russell come in as Oliver readies for the Plantation.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: The plantation, did the Lincoln Garden burn down about that time? Can you remember somebody?

Well what I mean, the Lincoln Garden had had a fire in there while we was working there. But then they built it up right up. When it went out on the road then it built back up. Right. But later on, after the band was out of there, it really burnt down completely. But Jo then was working in there.
Can you tell a bit more about that band? There's some other New Orleans fellows in there too, I believe the clarinetists.
Well now, you see when he first started man, he sent the walls and got Albert Nicholas. Well now when he first started Lincoln Garden we had Buster Bailey and Rudy Jackson. Oh yeah.
Sax, they played bass or baritone sax? No, no, Charlie Jackson.

Now it was him and Rudy Jackson, the tenor saxophone player. Oh yeah, I never did get that straight. Rudy Jackson, the tenor saxophone player, he's here now driving taxidale. Yeah, I knew he was right. And Buster Bailey's playing there. Then Charlie Jackson, he played bass saxophone. And Joe started experimenting with the bass saxophone. You see, and he had a, oh, I see, we were playing trombone. Cause we was changing trombone so much until he got what we want.
I remember one picture they had Zoo Robertson, do you remember Zoo?

Yeah, Zoo was there at one time. He was there at one time? Yeah, yeah, that's right. He's dead now. Then they had this other boy, Eddie Atkins was in there. And, uh, well, it's hard to say because, I mean, we've changed the trombone. He changed the trombone.

Was Roy Palmer with you there? Yeah, Roy Palmer played it one time to a, to a thing. You see, because what he was trying to do, he was trying to get a good enough trombone player to take off, uh... Take Dutre's. Yes, sir. That's right. They take Dutre's pieces. Because real Billy's man, right? Yeah. Well then, during that time, Buster Bailey got an offer to go to New York. Yeah, but Henderson was that? That's right. And Rudy Jackson said he was going. Then Joe sent to New Orleans and got Bonnie Bigard and Albert Nicholas to come up to take the two saxophone places. Meanwhile, they knew of the piano player from Panama. Yeah. You know, Louis Russell. Yes, I knew him. So they said, well, we'll bring him on up here with us. Yeah. Well, see, then Joe was trying to strengthen the band up then, for he could get ready to go into the plantation. See, still thank you God, when he's still in the band, because they, Peyton was going to leave out of the plantation and go to Persian Palace. So he was out of 64th and go. And Joe was going to follow us in there. That's when he, that's the way he's still in this band right there. And then that's when he changed and got rid of Charlie Jackson, because Charlie Jackson got to be a little, the bass saxophone, but got to be a little bit of unbearable on things. And they got Bert Cobb. Oh yeah, Bert Cobb. Bert Cobb on bass horn. And Bert Cobb was the one that went in the plantation on Bert Cobb. And then there were, uh, uh, uh, uh, there was some of his place shows up there. And now that's, that's, that's what, uh, I mean, I never did get that straight from Joe. See, I and Joe used to talk with us, you know, we used to go, we had an exhaustive thing. I don't know why Joe changed Lee Collins and got Tommy Ladner.
